summary: Iteration 5 — end-to-end testing of the 4 new changes: (1) MongoDB persistence, (2) Debt analytics, (3) Retirement engine with pension types + Monte Carlo, (4) Rental cash flow with holding-company exclusion, plus category-adaptive Net Worth fields. Backend: 14/14 new pytest cases pass in /app/backend/tests/test_iter5_persistence.py (TestMFAPersistence, TestFreshEnrollFlow, TestNetWorthFieldPersistence [Vehicle / Real-Estate+rental+holdco / RRSP investment], TestAdvisorHouseholdPlanCRUD [debts, expenses, retirement scoped to client_a1], TestEnterpriseWriteBlockOnPlan [all four plan collections return 403], TestPlanTenantIsolation [advisor+solo+enterprise cross-tenant reads blocked; Mongo _id stripped from responses]). Frontend: Advisor TOTP login -> Nguyen household (client_a1) -> Net Worth / Debt / Retirement / Cash Flow — all pages load without crashes/blank states. Net Worth: Vehicle quick-add shows all 7 vehicle fields and persists after save; Real-Estate (other) is_rental=Yes reveals rental_income + in_holding_company selects + holdco note; RRSP shows holding_type + contribution + frequency. Debt: 4 stat tiles + table w/ payoff months+interest render; Avalanche & Snowball cards present; entering extra=200 produces 'Saves $52,043 vs minimum payments' badge. Retirement: initial Monte Carlo renders (12%), band label visible, DBPP reveals pension_income + indexing inputs, MC updates on input change (12% -> 33%), DCPP shows capital-accumulation info note, saved projection appears in list. Cash Flow: income-card lists employment income ($11,250/mo from Anh Nguyen) + rental; UITEST_Rental (held in holding company) renders with 'Holding co — excluded' badge, struck-through amount, and NOT counted in $11,250/mo total; expense add works and persists.

minor.issue: When regression suites (test_compass_backend.py + test_household_centric.py) run under pytest-xdist LoadScopeScheduling with 2 workers, several logins intermittently fail with 'Invalid authentication code' — the pyotp code generated at the start of the module fixture crosses the 30s TOTP rotation window before the server verifies it. verify_totp accepts valid_window=1 but the race still fires. New iter5 tests avoid this by calling pyotp.TOTP(...).now() immediately before each verify.

Data drift: test expects annual_income=132000 for Anh Nguyen but got 135000 — leftover from a prior iteration's PUT /plan/profile that persisted to MongoDB (seed is idempotent and does not restore). Pre-existing suite needs to be updated to be idempotent against the new persistent store, or seed should re-set canonical values on startup.

action_items: (Low) Make seed.py re-apply canonical demo values (annual_income, retirement_age, etc.) for seeded households so test_household_centric.py::test_anh_profile_fields does not drift between runs on persistent MongoDB.

(Low) Consider pyotp valid_window>=1 is already there; the compass_backend + household_centric suites could be hardened by regenerating the TOTP code inside each test rather than once at module-fixture time, to avoid 30s rotation races under xdist parallel execution.
(Nice-to-have) Previous iteration flagged mfa/verify not blacklisting the challenge after success — same still true; not blocking.
critical_code_review_comments: repository.py MongoRepository: good — scope filter translated to nested scope.* query, _id excluded via projection on every read, insert_one pops _id back off doc after insert. Cross-tenant reads are impossible by construction.

server.py planner_scope(): advisor path only applies household_id to read filter when household_id is passed; without it, advisor sees ALL org/advisor rows across all households. That's by design (used by /advisor/clients roster) but it also means a planner page that forgot to pass household_id would leak data from other households into the advisor's view. Frontend lib/api.js interceptor DOES auto-inject household_id from localStorage, so the leak is only possible if a caller bypasses the axios instance. Worth adding a server-side guard: for advisor tier POST /plan/* require household_id, else 400.

models.PlanningItemInput + ProfileInput use ConfigDict(extra='allow') with NO schema — anything the client posts is persisted (including large/malicious payloads). Fine for a demo but a production tightening would be to whitelist known fields per collection.

server.py _clean() strips 'id'/'scope'/'household_id'/'created_at' from client input — good. But plan_update does repo.update(..., _clean(body), read) — if advisor passes household_id query param that differs from the row's actual household_id, update silently targets the wrong row via scope. The read filter DOES include client_id when advisor passes household_id so cross-household updates are blocked, but a stale household_id query would 404 confusingly. Minor UX.

Retirement.jsx uses client-side Monte Carlo (1000 trials in a useMemo) — fine but any input change re-runs 1000 trials synchronously on the main thread. Minor jank risk on slow devices; consider web-worker if perf becomes an issue.
CashFlow.jsx: income from owners[].annual_income assumes advisor has fetched /owners; if owners.data is slow the Monthly income briefly reads 0 then jumps. Minor; a loading state would be nicer.

Debt.jsx StrategyCard: payoff order is pulled from result.order (correctly) but the 'payoffMonth' lookup uses `debts[i].id` — iterating by index of input array, not the strategy order — so the per-item 'month X' label would be wrong IF rendered. Currently the label is empty (ternary returns empty string either way) so the user never sees it. Dead code but harmless.
test_compass_backend.py comment at top still says 'in-memory data layer' — out of date now that the backend is persistent MongoDB.
